<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Let $R\subseteq2^{<\omega}$ be a tree such that $[R]=\{x\in2^{\omega}:\forall n\in\omega\textbf{ }x|_{[f(n),f(n+1))}\in A_{x|_{f(n)}}\}$. It follows that $[R]+Y\in\mathcal{E}$. Let $\{T_{m}:m\in\omega\}$ be such collection of trees on $2^{<\omega}$ that $[R]+Y\subseteq\bigcup_{n}[T_{m}]$ and every $[T_{m}]$ is of measure zero. By Baire category theorem we have that 
               \begin{center}
                   $\forall y\in Y$ $\exists\sigma\in R$ $\exists m\in\omega$ $[R|_{\sigma}]+y\subseteq[T_{m}]$
               \end{center}
            Thus, if $Y_{\sigma,m}=\{y\in Y:[R|_{\sigma}]+y\subseteq[T_{m}]\}$, then $Y=\bigcup_{\sigma,m}Y_{\sigma,m}$. To construct the required slalom $S=(S_{n})_{n\in\omega}$, for every $\sigma$ and $m$ we will first construct a slalom $S^{\sigma,m}=(S_{n}^{\sigma,m})_{n\in\omega}$ with $S_{n}^{\sigma,m}\subseteq2^{[f(n),f(n+1))}$ and $|S_{n}^{\sigma,m}|\leq 2^{n^{2}}$ such that
            \begin{center}
                $Y_{\sigma,m}\subseteq\{x\in2^{\omega}:\forall^\infty n\in\omega $ $y|_{[f(n),f(n+1))}\in S_{n}^{\sigma,m}\}$
            \end{center}
            When these slaloms are constructed, we define $S=(S_{n})_{n\in\omega}$ as a diagonal union over $S^{\sigma,m}$'s as follows: enumerate all pairs $(\sigma,m)\in R\times \omega$ as $\{(\sigma_{k},m_{k}):k\in\omega\}$ and then for every $n\in\omega$ define $S_{n}=\bigcup_{k\leq n}S^{\sigma_{k},m_{k}}_{n}$. Then, we clearly have that $|S_{n}|\leq n\cdot 2^{n^{2}}=g(n)$ and also $Y\subseteq\{x\in2^{\omega}:\forall^\infty n\in\omega$ $x|_{[f(n),f(n+1))}\in S_{n}\}$ This will finish the proof of the claim.\\
            To construct the slalom $S^{\sigma,m}$ fix $\sigma$ and $m$. For every $n\in\omega$ define
            \begin{center}
                $S_{n}^{\sigma,m}=\{y|_{[f(n),f(n+1))}:y\in Y_{\sigma,m}\}$
            \end{center}
            We only have to check that $|S_{n}^{\sigma,m}|\leq 2^{n^{2}}$. Let $\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}=\{y|_{f(n+1)}:y\in Y_{\sigma,m}\}$. As $|S_{n}^{\sigma,m}|\leq|\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}|$ we will only have to estimate the size of $\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}$. Let $N\in\omega$ be large enough so that $\frac{|T_{m}\cap 2^{n}|}{2^{n}}<\frac{1}{2}$ for every $n>N$. Then for such $n$'s we have that:
            \begin{center}
                $\bigcup_{y\in Y_{\sigma,m}}(R\cap 2^{f(n+1)})+y|_{f(n+1)}=\bigcup_{\tau\in \widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}}(R\cap 2^{f(n+1)})+\tau\subseteq T_{m}\cap 2^{f(n+1)}$
            \end{center}
            Thus we have that:
            \begin{center}
                $\vspace{8px}\frac{1}{2}\geq\mu(\bigcup_{y\in Y_{\sigma,m}}R\cap 2^{f(n+1)}+y|_{f(n+1)})=1-\mu(\bigcap_{\tau\in\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}}2^{\omega}\setminus[R\cap2^{f(n+1)}+\tau])\geq\newline \vspace{8px}\geq 1-\Pi_{\tau\in\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}}\mu(2^{\omega}\setminus[R\cap2^{f(n)}+\tau])=1-\Pi_{\tau\in\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}}[1-\mu([R\cap2^{f(n+1)}]+\tau)]=\newline=1-\Pi_{\tau\in\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}}[1-\frac{|R\cap2^{f(n+1)}|}{2^{f(n+1)}}]=1-[1-\Pi_{i=0}^{n}\frac{|A_{s_{i}}|}{2^{f(i+1)-f(i)}}]^{|\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}|}=1-[1-\Pi_{i=0}^{n}\frac{1}{2_{i}}(1-\frac{1}{2^{g_{i}}})]^{|\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}|}$
            \end{center}
            and then
            \begin{center}
                $\vspace{8px}\frac{1}{2}\leq(1-\Pi_{i=0}^{n}\frac{1}{2_{i}}(1-\frac{1}{2^{g_{i}}}))^{|\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}|}\leq(1-\Pi_{i=0}^{n}\frac{1}{2_{i}}(1-\frac{1}{2}))^{|\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}|}=\newline =[1-\frac{1}{2^{\Sigma_{i=0}^{n}(i+1)}}]^{|\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}|}\leq(1-\frac{1}{2^{n^{2}}})^{|\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}|}$
            \end{center}
            It follows that
            \begin{center} $|\widetilde{S}_{n}^{\sigma,m}|\leq2^{n^{2}}$
            \end{center}
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- claim-7: body_md -->
$Y+(2^{\omega}\setminus F)\neq 2^{\omega}$
<!-- end claim-7 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
According to the last item of the claim \ref{claimWithConditions}, for every $n\in\omega$, there is $\sigma^{*}_{n}\in 2^{[f(n),f(n+1))}$ such that $\sigma^{*}_{n}\notin S_{n}+(2^{[f(n),f(n+1))}\setminus B_{n})$. Define then $z=\sigma^{*}_{n}$$^{\frown}\sigma^{*}_{n}$$^{\frown}...$ in $2^{\omega}$. We claim that $z\notin Y+(2^{\omega}\setminus F)$. Suppose towards a contradiction that $z=y+x$ where $y\in Y$ and $x\notin F$. Then there is $n\in\omega$ such that $y|_{[f(n),f(n+1))}\in S_{n}$ and $x|_{[f(n),f(n+1))}\notin B_{n}$. This contradicts the fact that $(y+x)|_{[f(n),f(n+1))}=z|_{[f(n),f(n+1))}=\sigma^{*}_{n}\notin S_{n}+(2^{[f(n),f(n+1))}\setminus B_{n})$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- theorem-32: body_md -->
The following inequalities hold:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item[--] $\mathrm{non}(\mathcal{E}^{*})\leq\sup\{\mathfrak{d}(\Pi F,\in^{*},\mathcal{S}lm(F,b)):F\in\omega^{\omega},$ and $b\leq F\}$,
            \item[--] $\mathrm{non}(\mathcal{E}^{*})\geq\min\{\mathfrak{d}(\Pi F,\in^{*},\mathcal{S}lm(F,b)):F\in\omega^{\omega},$ and $b\leq F$, $\Sigma_{n}\frac{b(n)}{F(n)}<\infty\}$.
        \end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-32 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
To show the first inequality assume that $F,b\in\omega^{\omega}$ and that $\{S_{\alpha}:\alpha<\kappa\}$ is a collection of $(F,b)$-slaloms that witness for the $\mathfrak{d}(\Pi F,\in^{*},\mathcal{S}lm(F,b))$. Without loss of generality, we may enlarge $F$ and assume that $F(n)=2^{i_{n}}$ for some $i_{n}\in\omega$. Let now $(I_{n})_{n\in\omega}$ be such interval partition that $|I_{n}|=i_{n}$ for every $n\in\omega$. For $\alpha<\kappa$ define the set
        \begin{center}
            $F_{\alpha}=\{x\in2^{\omega}:\forall^\infty n\in\omega$ $x|_{I_{n}}\in S_{\alpha}(n)\}$
        \end{center}
        By the choice of $\{S_{\alpha}:\alpha<\kappa\}$ we have that $\bigcup_{\alpha<\kappa}F_{\alpha}$ covers $2^{\omega}$. Let $E\in\mathcal{E}$ be the set from the lemma \ref{LemmaTranslatinalE}. We need the following.
        \begin{claim}
            For every $\alpha<\kappa$ we have $F_{\alpha}+E\in\mathcal{E}$.
        \end{claim}
        \begin{proof}
            Recall the construction of the set $E$ from the lemma \ref{LemmaTranslatinalE}. Notice first that in the construction, we may assume that every interval $(I_{k})_{k\in\omega}$ is a union of the intervals $[f(n),f(n+1))$. Then we have that 
            \begin{center}
                $F_{\alpha}+E\subseteq\{x\in2^{\omega}:\forall^\infty n\in\omega$ $x|_{I_{n}}\in A_{x|_{f(n)}}+S_{\alpha}(n)|_{[f(n),f(n+1))}\}$
            \end{center}
            and the latter is an $F_{\sigma}$-set of measure zero. This finishes the proof of the claim.
        \end{proof}
        By the lemma \ref{LemmaTranslatinalE}, for every $\alpha<\kappa$ there is $y_{\alpha}\in 2^{\omega}$ such that $F_{\alpha}\subseteq E+y_{\alpha}$. We claim that the set $Y=\{y_{\alpha}:\alpha<\kappa\}$ is not in $\mathcal{E}^{*}$ because $Y+E=2^{\omega}$. To see this, let $x\in2^{\omega}$ be arbitrary. Then for some $\alpha<\kappa$, we have that
        \begin{center}
            $x\in F_{\alpha}\subseteq E+y_{\alpha}\subseteq E+Y$
        \end{center}
        This finishes the proof of the first inequality.\\
        To prove the second inequality, assume that for some $X\subseteq2^{\omega}$ and some $E\in\mathcal{E}$ we have $2^{\omega}=\bigcup_{x\in X}E+x$. Using the characterization \ref{CharacterizationE} of the $\sigma$-ideal $\mathcal{E}$, we may assume that for some interval partition $(I_{n})_{n\in\omega}$ and a slalom $(S_{n})_{n\in\omega}$ such that $S_{n}\subseteq 2^{I_{n}}$, $\frac{|S_{n}|}{2^{|I_{n}|}}\leq\frac{1}{2^{n}}$, the set $E$ is of the form $\{x\in2^{\omega}:\forall^\infty n\in\omega$ $x|_{I_{n}}\in S_{n}\}$. Let $F,b\in\omega^{\omega}$ be such that $F(n)=2^{|I_{n}|}$ and $b(n)=\frac{F(n)}{2^{n}}$. In this way, every element of $\Pi F$ naturally corresponds with a unique element of $2^{\omega}$.
        Now, if for $x\in X$, the slalom $(S^{x}_{n})_{n\in\omega}$ is defined as
        \begin{center}
            $S^{x}_{n}=\{i\in F(n): i$ corresponds with an element of $S_{n}+x|_{I_{n}}\}$
        \end{center}
        then clearly the collection $\{(S^{x}_{n})_{n\in\omega}:x\in X\}$ is a witness for $\mathfrak{d}(\Pi F,\in^{*},\mathcal{S}lm(F,b))$.
        This finishes the proof of the second inequality and the theorem.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- claim-8: body_md -->
For every $\alpha<\kappa$ we have $F_{\alpha}+E\in\mathcal{E}$.
<!-- end claim-8 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Recall the construction of the set $E$ from the lemma \ref{LemmaTranslatinalE}. Notice first that in the construction, we may assume that every interval $(I_{k})_{k\in\omega}$ is a union of the intervals $[f(n),f(n+1))$. Then we have that 
            \begin{center}
                $F_{\alpha}+E\subseteq\{x\in2^{\omega}:\forall^\infty n\in\omega$ $x|_{I_{n}}\in A_{x|_{f(n)}}+S_{\alpha}(n)|_{[f(n),f(n+1))}\}$
            \end{center}
            and the latter is an $F_{\sigma}$-set of measure zero. This finishes the proof of the claim.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
If a forcing notion $\mathbb{P}$ has the Laver property, then $\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}"2^{\omega}\cap\mathbb{V}\notin\mathcal{E}^{*}"$
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- question-5: body_md -->
\label{QuestionSlalomNumbersVsNons}
        Are the following equalities true in ZFC?
        \begin{itemize}
            \item[--] $\mathrm{non}(\langle\mathcal{E},\mathcal{M}\rangle)=\sup\{\mathfrak{d}(\Pi F,=^{\infty},\Pi F):F\in\omega^{\omega}\}$,
            \item[--] $\mathrm{non}(\mathcal{E}^{*})=\sup\{\mathfrak{d}(\Pi F,\in^{*},Slm(F)):F\in\omega^{\omega}\}$.
        \end{itemize}
<!-- end question-5 -->
<!-- question-6: body_md -->
Are the following equalities true in ZFC?
        \begin{itemize}
            \item[--] $\mathrm{add}(\mathcal{MA})=\mathrm{add}(\mathcal{M})$ (Cardona, Mejía and Rivera-Madrid),
            \item[--] $\mathrm{add}(\langle\mathcal{E},\mathcal{M}\rangle)=\mathrm{add}(\mathcal{M})$.
        \end{itemize}
<!-- end question-6 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
For a $\sigma$-ideal $\mathcal{I}$ on $2^{\omega}$ define: 
            \begin{itemize}
                \item[--] $\mathrm{add}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{I})=\min\{|\mathcal{F}|:\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{I}$ and $\neg\exists X\in\mathcal{I}$ $\forall F\in\mathcal{F}$ $\exists x\in2^{\omega}$ $F+x\subseteq X\}$
                \item[--] $\mathrm{cof}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{I})=\min\{|\mathcal{F}|:\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{I}$ and $\forall Y\in\mathcal{I}$ $\exists Y'\in\mathcal{F}$ $\exists x\in2^{\omega}$ $Y\subseteq Y'+x\}$
            \end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- theorem-33: body_md -->
(Pawlikowski; \cite{PawlikowskiTransitiveInvariants})
            The following holds:
            \begin{itemize}
                \item[--] $\mathrm{add}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{N})=\mathrm{add}(\mathcal{N})$,
                \item[--] $\mathrm{cof}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{N})=\mathrm{cof}(\mathcal{N})$,
                \item[--] $\mathrm{add}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{M})=\mathfrak{b}$,
                \item[--] $\mathrm{cof}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{M})=\mathfrak{d}$.
            \end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-33 -->
<!-- theorem-34: body_md -->
The following inequalities hold:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item[--] $\mathrm{add}(\mathcal{M})\leq\mathrm{add}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{E})\leq\mathfrak{b}$,
            \item[--] $\mathfrak{d}\leq\mathrm{cof}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{E})\leq\mathrm{cof}(\mathcal{M})$.
            \end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-34 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
First, we notice that $\mathrm{add}(\mathcal{M})\leq\mathrm{add}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{E})$ and $\mathrm{cof}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{E})\leq\mathrm{cof}(\mathcal{M})$ easily follows from the observation above and the fact that $\mathrm{add}(\mathcal{E})=\mathrm{add}(\mathcal{M})$ and $\mathrm{cof}(\mathcal{E})=\mathrm{cof}(\mathcal{M})$ (see Theorem \ref{CardInvsofE}).\\
            To show that $\mathrm{add}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{E})\leq\mathfrak{b}$ let $\{f_{\alpha}:\alpha<\mathfrak{b}\}\subseteq\omega^{\omega}$ be an unbounded family of increasing functions. For every $\alpha<\mathfrak{b}$ let $T_{\alpha}\subseteq2^{<\omega}$ be the tree that splits only on levels $n\in\omega\setminus rng(f_{\alpha})$ and picks $0$ elsewhere. Clearly, $E_{\alpha}=[T_{\alpha}]\in E$ and for every $n\in\omega$ we have 
            \begin{center}
                $\frac{|T_{\alpha}\cap 2^{f_{\alpha}(n)}|}{2^{f_{\alpha}(n)}}=\frac{1}{2^{n}}$
            \end{center}
            Assume that $E=\bigcup_{n}F_{n}$ is such that each $F_{n}$ is closed set of measure zero and that for every $\alpha<\mathfrak{b}$ there is $x_{\alpha}\in 2^{\omega}$ such that $E_{\alpha}+x_{\alpha}\subseteq E$. By Baire category theorem for every $\alpha$ there are $\sigma\in 2^{<\omega}$ and $n_{\alpha}\in\omega$ such that $[T_{\alpha}+x_{\alpha}|_{\sigma_{\alpha}}]\subseteq F_{n_{\alpha}}$. Without loss of generality, we may assume that all $\sigma_{\alpha}$'s and $n_{\alpha}$'s are the same and are equal $\sigma$ and $n$. Let $T\subseteq2^{<\omega}$ be such tree that $F_{n}=[T]$ and let $g\in\omega^{\omega}$ be such that for every $n\in\omega$ for every $m>g(n)$ we have
            \begin{center}
                $\frac{|T\cap 2^{m}|}{2^{m}}<\frac{1}{2^{n+|\sigma|}}$
            \end{center}    
            Let $\alpha<\mathfrak{b}$ be such that $g(n)<f_{\alpha}(n)$ for infinitely many $n$'s. But then for every such $n>|\sigma|$ we get 
            \begin{center}
                $\frac{1}{2^{n+|\sigma|}}
                =\frac{|(T_{\alpha}+x_{\alpha})|_{\sigma}|}{2^{f_{\alpha}(n)}}
                \leq\frac{|T\cap 2^{f_{\alpha}(n)|}}{2^{f_{\alpha}(n)}}
                <\frac{1}{2^{f_{\alpha}(n)}}$
            \end{center}
            which is the final contradiction.\\
            Next we show that $\mathfrak{d}\leq\mathrm{cof}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{E})$. Let $\{E_{\alpha}:\alpha<\kappa\}\subseteq\mathcal{E}$ where $\kappa<\mathfrak{d}$. We will construct a set $E\in\mathcal{E}$ such that no translation of any $E_{\alpha}$ covers $E$. By Proposition \ref{CharacterizationE}, without loss of generality, we may assume that for every $\alpha<\kappa$ there is an interval partition $(I^{\alpha}_{n})_{n\in\omega}$ and a slalom $S^{\alpha}=(S^{\alpha}(n))_{n\in\omega}$ such that 
            \begin{center}
                $E_{\alpha}\subseteq\{x\in2^{\omega}:\forall^\infty n\in\omega\textbf{ }x|_{I^{\alpha}_{n}}\in S^{\alpha}(n)\}$
            \end{center}
            As $\kappa<\mathfrak{d}$, there is an interval partition $(J_{k})_{k<\omega}$ not dominated by any $(I^{\alpha}_{n})_{n\in\omega}$. For $i=0,1$ let $T_{i}\subseteq2^{<\omega}$ be such tree that $\sigma\in split(T_{i})$ if and only if $|\sigma|\notin\{\min J_{2k+i}:k<\omega\}$. Define $E=[T_{0}]\cup[T_{1}]$. Clearly $E\in\mathcal{E}$. Suppose that $E\subseteq E_{\alpha}+y=\{x\in2^{\omega}:x|_{I^{\alpha}_{n}}\in S^{\alpha}(n)+y|_{I^{\alpha}_{n}}\}$. Then there are infinitely many intervals $I^{\alpha}_{n}$ covered by $J_{k}\cup J_{k+1}$. Let $i\in 2$ be the parity of infinitely many of these $k$'s. Then it is easy to construct $z\in[T_{i}]$ such that $z|_{I^{\alpha}_{n}}\notin S^{\alpha}(n)+y|_{I^{\alpha}_{n}}$ for infinitely many $n\in\omega$. Clearly, then $z\in E\setminus (E_{\alpha}+y)$.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- question-7: body_md -->
Is $\mathrm{add}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{E})=\mathrm{add}(\mathcal{M})$ and $\mathrm{cof}^{*}_{t}(\mathcal{E})=\mathrm{cof}(\mathcal{M})$?
<!-- end question-7 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be a $\sigma$-ideal on $2^{\omega}$. An uncountable set $X\subseteq2^{\omega}$ is $\mathcal{I}$-Luzin set if the intersection $X\cap F$ is countable for any $F\in\mathcal{I}$.
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- theorem-35: body_md -->
(Pawlikowski; \cite{PawlikowskiSierpinski})\label{SierpIsStrMeager}
        Every Sierpiński set is strongly meager.
<!-- end theorem-35 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
A set $X\subseteq2^{\omega}$ has the Menger property if for every continuous function $f:X\rightarrow\omega^{\omega}$, the image $f[X]$ is not dominating.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{SierpińskiHASMenger}
        Every $\mathcal{E}$-Luzin set has the Menger property.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Let $f:2^{\omega}\rightarrow\omega^{\omega}$ be a continuous function and let $L\subseteq2^{\omega}$ be an $\mathcal{E}$-Luzin set. For every $n\in\omega$ pick $g(n)\in\omega$ be such that the clopen set 
        \begin{center}
            $F_{n}=:\bigcup_{m>g(n)}f^{-1}[\{x\in\omega^{\omega}:x(n)=m\}]$
        \end{center}
        is of measure $<\frac{1}{2^{n}}$. Then the set $E=:\{x\in2^{\omega}:\forall^\infty n\in\omega$ $x\in F_{n}\}$ is $F_{\sigma}$-set of measure zero. As $L\cap E$ is countable, we have that 
        \begin{center}
            $L\setminus E\subseteq\{x\in2^{\omega}:\exists^\infty n\in\omega$ $f(x)(n)\leq g(n)\}$
        \end{center}
        It follows that $f[L\setminus E]$ does not dominate $g\in\omega^{\omega}$. We can then improve $g$ so we dominate this countably many exceptions. This finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- question-8: body_md -->
Is it true that for any $\mathcal{E}$-Luzin set $X\subseteq2^{\omega}$ and any Borel function $f:X\rightarrow\omega^{\omega}$ the image $f[X]$ does not form a dominating family?
<!-- end question-8 -->
<!-- theorem-36: body_md -->
Every $\mathcal{E}$-Luzin is in $\mathcal{E}^{*}$.
<!-- end theorem-36 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Let $L\subseteq2^{\omega}$ be an $\mathcal{E}$-Luzin set and let $E\in\mathcal{E}$. We are looking for a point $z$ outside of the set $L+E$. Assume that $\{T_{n}:n\in\omega\}$ is a sequence of trees on $2^{<\omega}$ such that $E\subseteq\bigcup_{n\in\omega}[T_{n}]$ and every $[T_{n}]$ is of measure zero. Let $Q=\{q_{n}:n\in\omega\}\in[\omega]^{\omega}$ be such that for every $n\in\omega$ for every $m>q_{n}$ we have $\frac{|T_{n}\cap2^{m}|}{2^{m}}<\frac{1}{2^{n}}$. For $l\in2^{\omega}$ and $n\in\omega$ we define
        \begin{center}
            $S^{l}_{n}=(T_{n}\cap 2^{q_{n}})+l|_{q_{n}}$
        \end{center}
        Note that $L+E\subseteq\bigcup_{l\in L}E_{l}$ where $E_{l}=\{y\in2^{\omega}:\forall^\infty_{n\in\omega}$ $ y|_{q_{n}}\in S^{l}_{n}\}\in\mathcal{E}$. For $n,k\in\omega$ and $l\in L$ define 
        \begin{equation*}
            \begin{aligned}
            F^{l}_{n}(k)=\{\langle\sigma_{0},...,\sigma_{k}\rangle\in(2^{q_{n}})^{k+1}:&\exists 0\leq \tilde{q}_{0}\leq...\leq\tilde{q}_{k-1}\leq q_{n} \text{ with all } \tilde{q}_{i}\in Q\\
             & \text{and }\sigma_{0}|_{\tilde{q}_{0}}\cup \sigma_{1}|_{[\tilde{q}_{0},\tilde{q}_{1})}\cup...\cup \sigma_{k}|_{[\tilde{q}_{k-1},q_{n})}\in S^{l}_{n}\}
            \end{aligned}
        \end{equation*}
        In such case will say that such the sequence $\langle\sigma_{0},...,\sigma_{k}\rangle\in(2^{q_{n}})^{k+1}$ has a diagonal in $S^{l}_{n}$. Define now the following sets
        \begin{center}
            $F^{l}(k)=\{\langle x_{0},...,x_{k}\rangle\in(2^{\omega})^{k+1}: \forall^\infty n\in\omega$ $\langle x_{0}|_{q_{n}},x_{1}|_{q_{n}},...,x_{k}|_{q_{n}}\rangle\in F^{l}_{n}(k)\}$,
        \end{center}
        \begin{center}
            $F^{l}=\{\langle x_{0},x_{1},....\rangle\in(2^{\omega})^{\omega}:\exists k\in\omega$ $\langle x_{0},...,x_{k}\rangle\in F^{l}(k)\}$
        \end{center}
        Let now $F\subseteq2^{\omega}\times(2^{\omega})^{\omega}$ be such that the vertical section of $F$ above $l\in2^{\omega}$ is equal $F^{l}$ i.e. $F=\{(l,\langle x_{k}:k\in\omega\rangle)\in2^{\omega}\times(2^{\omega})^{\omega}:\langle x_{k}:k\in\omega\rangle\in F^{l}\}$. We will need the following claim.
        \begin{claim}
            $F$ is an $F_{\sigma}$-set with all vertical sections of measure zero.
        \end{claim}
        \begin{proof}
            Clearly $F$ a an $F_{\sigma}$-set. To see that its sections are of measure zero let us first estimate the sizes of sets $F^{l}_{n}(k)$. Let $l\in2^{\omega}$. First notice that there are less than $(1+n)^{k}$ choices for the sequence $0\leq \tilde{q}_{0}\leq...\leq\tilde{q}_{k-1}\leq q_{n} \text{ with all } \tilde{q}_{i}\in Q$. There are also $|S^{l}_{n}|$ choices for the diagonal sequence $\sigma_{0}|_{\tilde{q}_{0}}\cup \sigma_{1}|_{[\tilde{q}_{0},\tilde{q}_{1})}\cup...\cup \sigma_{k}|_{[\tilde{q}_{k-1},q_{n})}$. It follows that
            \begin{center}
                $|F^{l}_{n}(k)|\leq(1+n)^{k}\cdot |S^{l}_{n}|\cdot 2^{(q_{n}-q_{0})}\cdot2^{(q_{n}-q_{1}+q_{0})}\cdot...\cdot2^{(q_{n}-q_{n}+q_{k-1})}=(1+n)^{k}\cdot |S^{l}_{n}|\cdot (2^{q_{n}})^{k-1}$
            \end{center}
            Thus we have 
            \begin{center}
                $\vspace{10px}\mu(\{\langle x_{0},x_{1},...,x_{k}\rangle\in(2^{\omega})^{k+1}:\forall n\in\omega$ $\langle x_{0}|_{q_{n}},x_{1}|_{q_{n}},...,x_{k}|_{q_{n}}\rangle\in F^{x}_{n}\})\leq\newline\vspace{10px}\leq\mu(\{\langle x_{0},x_{1},...,x_{k}\rangle\in(2^{\omega})^{k+1}:\forall n\in\omega$ $\langle x_{0}|_{q_{n}},x_{1}|_{q_{n}},...,x_{k}|_{q_{n}}\rangle\in F^{x}_{n}\})\leq\newline\leq\frac{|F^{x}_{n}(k)|}{(2^{q_{n}})^{k+1}}=\frac{(1+n)^{k}\cdot |F^{x}_{n}|\cdot (2^{q_{n}})^{k-1}}{(2^{q_{n}})^{k+1}}\leq\frac{(1+n)^{k}\cdot |F^{x}_{n}|}{2^{q_{n}}}\leq\frac{(1+n)^{k}}{2^{n}}$
            \end{center}
            and the last item goes to zero with $n$ going to infinity.
        \end{proof}
        We will now inductively construct sequences
        \begin{itemize}
            \item[--] $\langle z_{k}:k\in\omega\rangle\in(2^{\omega})^{\omega}$,
            \item[--] $\{L_{k}:k\in\omega\}$, a partition of $L$ such that $|L_{k}|=\omega$ for $k\geq1$, and
            \item[--] $\{D_{k}\subseteq2^{\omega}:k\in\omega\}$ of sets of measure zero.
        \end{itemize}
        Before we proceed with the induction we will need the following notation. For any $k\in\omega$, $\langle x_{0},...,x_{k}\rangle\in(2^{\omega})^{k+1}$ and $l\in2^{\omega}$ define the sets
            \begin{center}
                $F^{l}_{\langle x_{0},...,x_{k}\rangle}=\{\langle x_{k+1},x_{k+2},...\rangle\in(2^{\omega})^{\omega\setminus (k+1)}:\langle x_{0},...,x_{k},x_{k+1},...\rangle\in F^{l}\}$,\\
                $C^{l}_{\langle x_{0},...,x_{k}\rangle}=\{x_{k+1}\in2^{\omega}:\mu(F^{l}_{\langle x_{0},...,x_{k},x_{k+1}\rangle})>0\}$
            \end{center}
            and
            \begin{center}
                $F_{\langle x_{0},...,x_{k}\rangle}=\{(l,\langle x_{k+1},...\rangle)\in2^{\omega}\times(2^{\omega})^{\omega\setminus(k+1)}:\langle x_{k+1},x_{k+2},...\rangle\in F^{l}_{\langle x_{0},...,x_{k}\rangle}\}$,\\
                $C_{\langle x_{0},...,x_{k}\rangle}=\{(l,x_{k+1})\in2^{\omega}\times2^{\omega}:x_{k+1}\in C^{l}_{\langle x_{0},...,x_{k}\rangle}\}$
            \end{center}
            Observe that the set $C_{\langle x_{0},...,x_{k}\rangle}$ is an $F_{\sigma}$-set. This is because for any $F_{\sigma}$ subset of the plane the set of those vertical sections that are of measure zero, is an $F_{\sigma}$-set.\\
        
        
        
        
        Start the induction by applying Fubini's theorem to the set $C_{\langle\rangle}$ to find $z_{0}\in2^{\omega}$ such that the set $D_{0}=\{l\in2^{\omega}:z_{0}\in C_{\langle\rangle}\}$ is null (and $F_{\sigma}$ by the observation above). Then the set $L_{1}=L\cap D_{0}$ is countable as $L$ is $\mathcal{E}$-Luzin. Assume now that $z_{k}$, $L_{k+1}$ and $D_{k}$ have been constructed. Apply Fubini's theorem to the set $C_{\langle z_{0},...,z_{k}\rangle}$ (which is an $F_{\sigma}$-set in $2^{\omega}\times2^{\omega}$ with horizontal sections in $\mathcal{E}$) to find a point 
        \begin{center}
            $z_{k+1}\in2^{\omega}\setminus(\bigcup_{l\in L_{1}}C^{l}_{\langle z_{1},...,z_{k}\rangle}\cup\bigcup_{l\in L_{2}}C^{l}_{\langle z_{2},...,z_{k}\rangle}\cup...\cup\bigcup_{l\in L_{k}}C^{l}_{\langle z_{k}\rangle}\cup\bigcup_{l\in L_{k+1}}C^{l}_{\langle\rangle})$
        \end{center}
        such that the set $D_{k+1}$ defined as $\{l\in2^{\omega}:z_{k+1}\in C^{l}_{\langle z_{0},z_{1},...,z_{k}\rangle}\}$ is of measure zero (and $F_{\sigma}$ by the preceding observation). Let then $L_{k+2}=(L\setminus \bigcup_{i\leq k+1}L_{i})\cap D_{k+1}$, which is a countable set as $L$ is $\mathcal{E}$-Luzin. This finishes the induction step. When the whole induction is over let $L_{0}=L\setminus \bigcup_{k\geq 1}L_{k}$.\\
        Note that the induction was performed in a way that 
        \begin{center}
            $\forall i\in\omega$ $(l\in L_{i}\rightarrow\forall k\geq i$ $z_{k+1}\notin C^{l}_{\langle z_{i},...,z_{k}\rangle})$
        \end{center}
        \begin{claim}
            If $l\in L_{i}$ and $k\geq i$, then $\exists^{\infty}q\in Q$ $\langle z_{i}|_{q},...,z_{k+1}|_{q}\rangle\notin F^{l}_{q}(k+1-i)$
        \end{claim}
        \begin{proof}[proof of the claim]
            Suppose otherwise: that for some $i\leq k$ and $l\in L_{i}$ for almost all $q\in Q$ we have that $\langle z_{i}|_{q},...,z_{k+1}|_{q}\rangle\in F^{l}_{q}(k+1-i)$. This means that $\langle z_{i}|_{q},...,z_{k+1}|_{q}\rangle\in F^{l}(k+1-i)$. On the other hand we have that $F^{l}_{\langle z_{i},...,z_{k+1}\rangle}=(2^{\omega})^{\omega\setminus(k+1-i)}$ which in particular means that $\mu(F^{l}_{\langle z_{i},...,z_{k}\rangle^{\frown}z_{k+1}})>0$. It follows that $z_{k+1}\in C^{l}_{\langle z_{i},...,z_{k}\rangle}$ which contradicts the preceding condition and thus proves the claim.
        \end{proof}
        Fix $l\in L_{i}$ and $i\leq k$. Let $Q^{l}_{k}\in[Q]^{\omega}$ be such that for all $q\in Q^{l}_{k}$ we have $\langle z_{i}|_{q},...,z_{k+1}|_{q}\rangle\notin F^{l}_{q}(k+1-i)$. Let $\{q^{l}_{k}:k\in\omega\}\in\omega^{\omega}$ be such sequence that $q^{l}_{k}$ is minimal with $|Q^{l}_{k}\cap q^{l}_{k}|=k+1-i$ for each $k\in\omega$.\\
        Define then $f:L\rightarrow \omega^{\omega}$ such that $f(l)(k)=q^{l}_{k}$. As the assignment $l\mapsto \{S^{l}_{k}:k\in\omega\}$ is continuous, the map $f$ is continuous as well. By the Lemma \ref{SierpińskiHASMenger} $f[L]$ is not a dominating family in $\omega^{\omega}$ so there is a $\{q_{k}:k\in\omega\}\in\omega^{\omega}$ such that for every $l\in L$ there are infinitely many $k\in\omega$ with $q^{l}_{k}\leq q_{k}$.\\
        Define now 
        \begin{center}
            $z=z_{0}|_{q_{0}}\cup z_{1}|_{[q_{0},q_{1})}\cup z_{2}|_{[q_{1},q_{2})}\cup...$
        \end{center}
        We will finish the proof by showing that $z\notin L+E$ so let $l\in L_{i}$ for some $i\in\omega$. It will suffice to show that the point $z'=z_{i}|_{q_{i}}\cup z_{i+1}|_{[q_{i},q_{i+1})}\cup...$ (which is a finite modification of $z$) is such that $z'|_{q}\notin S^{l}_{q}$ for infinitely many $q\in Q$. Let $A\in[\omega]^{\omega}$ be such that $q^{l}_{q}\leq q_{k}$ for every $k\in A$. For every $k\in A$ there is the biggest $q\leq q_{k}$, $q\in Q^{l}_{k}$. In particular for such $q\in Q^{l}_{k}\cap q_{k}$ we have $\langle z_{i}|_{q},...,z_{k+1}|_{q}\rangle\notin F^{l}_{q}(k+1-i)$ which means that $\langle z_{i}|_{q},...,z_{k+1}|_{q}\rangle$ does not have diagonal in $S^{l}_{q}$. In particular $z'|_{q}\notin S^{l}_{q}$ for every $k\in A$. This completes the proof of the theorem.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- claim-9: body_md -->
$F$ is an $F_{\sigma}$-set with all vertical sections of measure zero.
<!-- end claim-9 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Clearly $F$ a an $F_{\sigma}$-set. To see that its sections are of measure zero let us first estimate the sizes of sets $F^{l}_{n}(k)$. Let $l\in2^{\omega}$. First notice that there are less than $(1+n)^{k}$ choices for the sequence $0\leq \tilde{q}_{0}\leq...\leq\tilde{q}_{k-1}\leq q_{n} \text{ with all } \tilde{q}_{i}\in Q$. There are also $|S^{l}_{n}|$ choices for the diagonal sequence $\sigma_{0}|_{\tilde{q}_{0}}\cup \sigma_{1}|_{[\tilde{q}_{0},\tilde{q}_{1})}\cup...\cup \sigma_{k}|_{[\tilde{q}_{k-1},q_{n})}$. It follows that
            \begin{center}
                $|F^{l}_{n}(k)|\leq(1+n)^{k}\cdot |S^{l}_{n}|\cdot 2^{(q_{n}-q_{0})}\cdot2^{(q_{n}-q_{1}+q_{0})}\cdot...\cdot2^{(q_{n}-q_{n}+q_{k-1})}=(1+n)^{k}\cdot |S^{l}_{n}|\cdot (2^{q_{n}})^{k-1}$
            \end{center}
            Thus we have 
            \begin{center}
                $\vspace{10px}\mu(\{\langle x_{0},x_{1},...,x_{k}\rangle\in(2^{\omega})^{k+1}:\forall n\in\omega$ $\langle x_{0}|_{q_{n}},x_{1}|_{q_{n}},...,x_{k}|_{q_{n}}\rangle\in F^{x}_{n}\})\leq\newline\vspace{10px}\leq\mu(\{\langle x_{0},x_{1},...,x_{k}\rangle\in(2^{\omega})^{k+1}:\forall n\in\omega$ $\langle x_{0}|_{q_{n}},x_{1}|_{q_{n}},...,x_{k}|_{q_{n}}\rangle\in F^{x}_{n}\})\leq\newline\leq\frac{|F^{x}_{n}(k)|}{(2^{q_{n}})^{k+1}}=\frac{(1+n)^{k}\cdot |F^{x}_{n}|\cdot (2^{q_{n}})^{k-1}}{(2^{q_{n}})^{k+1}}\leq\frac{(1+n)^{k}\cdot |F^{x}_{n}|}{2^{q_{n}}}\leq\frac{(1+n)^{k}}{2^{n}}$
            \end{center}
            and the last item goes to zero with $n$ going to infinity.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- claim-10: body_md -->
If $l\in L_{i}$ and $k\geq i$, then $\exists^{\infty}q\in Q$ $\langle z_{i}|_{q},...,z_{k+1}|_{q}\rangle\notin F^{l}_{q}(k+1-i)$
<!-- end claim-10 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Suppose otherwise: that for some $i\leq k$ and $l\in L_{i}$ for almost all $q\in Q$ we have that $\langle z_{i}|_{q},...,z_{k+1}|_{q}\rangle\in F^{l}_{q}(k+1-i)$. This means that $\langle z_{i}|_{q},...,z_{k+1}|_{q}\rangle\in F^{l}(k+1-i)$. On the other hand we have that $F^{l}_{\langle z_{i},...,z_{k+1}\rangle}=(2^{\omega})^{\omega\setminus(k+1-i)}$ which in particular means that $\mu(F^{l}_{\langle z_{i},...,z_{k}\rangle^{\frown}z_{k+1}})>0$. It follows that $z_{k+1}\in C^{l}_{\langle z_{i},...,z_{k}\rangle}$ which contradicts the preceding condition and thus proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- question-9: body_md -->
Is every $\mathcal{I}$-Luzin in $\mathcal{I}^{*}$ for other $\sigma$-ideals $\mathcal{I}$ like $\sigma$-porosity ideal or the infinitely equal and eventually different ideals investigated in \cite{KhomskiiLaguzzi}. What about the $\sigma$-ideals of $\sigma$-compact (or not strongly dominating) subsets of $\mathbb{Z}^{\omega}$? Is there a natural example of $\sigma$-ideal $\mathcal{I}$, so that some $\mathcal{I}$-Luzin set is not $\mathcal{I}^{*}$?
<!-- end question-9 -->
